motivation: Nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions on curved domains are challenging to solve numerically, especially when the solution has low regularity. Existing methods lack rigorous convergence guarantees in this setting.
method: The method combines isoparametric bulk-surface finite elements with an exponential integrator in time. A weak-norm framework using lift and adjoint-lift operators handles the non-conforming geometry.
result: First-order convergence in time and spatial convergence of order h^{r+1/2} for r≥1 and h^{3/2} for r=0 are proved, showing higher-order elements retain advantage even at low regularity.
conclusion: This is the first fully discrete low-regularity convergence result for such problems, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates and efficiency of higher-order methods.

title: Convergence And Almost Sure Exponential Stability Of Compensated Split-step Theta Scheme For Stochastic Pantograph Models With Poisson Random Measure
authors: Amr Abosenna, Yongchun Zhou, Boping Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, stochastic pantograph models have gained an intensive attention and have been used in different fields such as finance, biology, control and stochastic neural networks. It is also more preferable to incorporate jumps during the study of stochastic differential equations. In this paper, stochastic pantograph model with Poisson random measure is studied. The compensated split-step theta technique is applied to the considered model. The numerical scheme exhibits a non divergent attitude and converges to the solution of our model under assumptions addressed later on. Furthermore, the almost sure exponential stability of the numerical scheme is investigated via utilizing the discrete semi-martingale convergence theorem. Finally, theoretical findings are manifested via some numerical examples.
tldr: This paper studies the convergence and stability of a numerical scheme for stochastic pantograph models with jumps, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Stochastic pantograph models with Poisson jumps are used in finance, biology, and neural networks, but the paper focuses on numerical analysis rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The compensated split-step theta scheme is applied to the stochastic pantograph model, and the discrete semi-martingale convergence theorem is used to prove almost sure exponential stability.
result: The numerical scheme converges to the solution under certain assumptions and is almost surely exponentially stable.
conclusion: The theoretical findings are supported by numerical examples, but the work has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Harq For Slow Fluid Antenna Multiple Access
authors: Sixu Han, Kai-Kit Wong, Hanjiang Hong, Hyundong Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slow fluid antenna multiple access (sFAMA), enabled by the fluid antenna system (FAS), has recently emerged as a practical and low-complexity paradigm for supporting massive wireless connectivity. While existing studies have characterized its physical-layer performance under one-shot transmission, its interaction with retransmission protocols and the resulting networking performance remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we study a downlink hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)-assisted sFAMA framework, termed HARQ-sFAMA, in which each user performs distinguished port selection in every HARQ round and combines the received signals across multiple rounds to improve decoding reliability. We develop a comprehensive analytical framework to characterize the outage probability, average packet waiting time, and energy efficiency of the proposed system. The analysis reveals how HARQ exploits the spatial reconfigurability of FAS to simultaneously enhance reliability and improve queueing performance. Numerical results corroborate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate that the HARQ-sFAMA system significantly outperforms conventional one-shot sFAMA in terms of reliability, delay, and energy efficiency. These findings suggest that the integration of HARQ and sFAMA provides a promising pathway toward a practical and standards-compatible massive access solution for future wireless networks.
tldr: This paper studies a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) protocol for slow fluid antenna multiple access (sFAMA) in wireless communications.
motivation: The interaction between retransmission protocols and sFAMA has not been explored, and the networking performance of sFAMA under HARQ is unknown.
method: The authors develop an analytical framework to characterize outage probability, average packet waiting time, and energy efficiency for the proposed HARQ-sFAMA system.
result: HARQ-sFAMA significantly outperforms conventional one-shot sFAMA in reliability, delay, and energy efficiency.
conclusion: Integrating HARQ with sFAMA provides a promising pathway toward practical massive access solutions for future wireless networks.

title: A National-Scale Ev Charging Scheduling Framework: Optimal Detour Routing Under Infrastructure Capacity Constraints
authors: Taner Cokyasar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption grows, quantifying the scheduling burden and economic cost of long-distance travel under the existing charging infrastructure becomes increasingly important for infrastructure planning and policy. This paper presents a scalable, optimization-based framework for scheduling EV charging stops along real-world charging stations and simulated long-distance personal vehicle trajectories across the United States using POLARIS. Taking the existing charging network as fixed input, the framework minimizes total detour and queuing costs for each vehicle while respecting plug capacity constraints at each station. The methodology proceeds in three phases: (i) infeasibility pruning via a forward-pass reachability heuristic, (ii) per-vehicle optimal charging schedule computation via dynamic programming on a directed acyclic graph, and (iii) capacity-aware iterative congestion resolution through a penalty-based heuristic that augments detour costs at congested stations, with a first-in, first-out queue fallback. Applied to approximately 2.7M origin--destination vehicle trajectories derived from a 1\% sample of national personal travel demand within the POLARIS agent-based transportation simulation framework and covering 14,260 DC fast charging stations with 68,641 plugs from the Alternative Fuels Station Locator, the framework produces capacity-feasible schedules in under 1.3 hours on a 128-core high-performance computing cluster without requiring any commercial optimization solver. A three-tier economic analysis spanning operational costs, total cost of ownership, and amortized infrastructure investment is conducted to evaluate EV cost competitiveness relative to internal combustion engine vehicles across scenarios.
tldr: This paper presents an optimization framework for scheduling electric vehicle charging stops on long-distance trips, considering detour and queuing costs under infrastructure capacity constraints.
motivation: As EV adoption grows, there is a need to quantify the scheduling burden and economic cost of long-distance travel under existing charging infrastructure to inform planning and policy.
method: The framework uses a three-phase approach: infeasibility pruning via reachability heuristic, per-vehicle optimal scheduling via dynamic programming on a DAG, and capacity-aware iterative congestion resolution with penalty-based heuristics and FIFO queue fallback.
result: Applied to 2.7M trajectories and 14,260 stations, the framework produces capacity-feasible schedules in under 1.3 hours on a 128-core cluster without commercial solvers.
conclusion: The framework enables large-scale EV charging scheduling and economic analysis, demonstrating feasibility for national-scale infrastructure planning.

title: Block Diagonal Carleson Frames
authors: Brendan Miller Ilya Krishtal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce , i.e. singly generated dynamical frames in which the generating operator is block diagonal. We classify all such frames when the generating operator is a direct sum of Jordan blocks, the sizes of which are uniformly bounded. Furthermore, block diagonal Carleson frames are shown to enjoy the high redundancy properties observed for Carleson frames. When the generating operator has nonnegative spectrum, we provide a complete description of the redundancy of such frames under the assumption of the existence of natural density.
tldr: This paper introduces block diagonal Carleson frames, a class of dynamical frames with block diagonal generating operators, and studies their classification and redundancy properties.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of Carleson frames to a more general setting where the generating operator is block diagonal, which includes direct sums of Jordan blocks.
method: The paper provides a classification of all such frames when the generating operator is a direct sum of Jordan blocks with uniformly bounded sizes, and analyzes redundancy under nonnegative spectrum assumptions using natural density.
result: Block diagonal Carleson frames are shown to retain the high redundancy properties of standard Carleson frames, and a complete description of redundancy is given for operators with nonnegative spectrum.
conclusion: The work contributes to frame theory but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisit Escape Path For Infinite Unit Strip Forest And Unit Broadworm
authors: Zhipeng Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on our previous general computational solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-Forest Problem, we present a new approach and analytical formulas for the previously well-known escape path for the infinite unit-strip forest and unit broadworm by Zalgaller. Earlier studies addressed these problems exclusively through geometric methods. We reformulated the problem as an interval-cover problem and then formulated it as a constrained functional minimization problem. This constrained functional minimization can be directly discretized and subsequently solved as a convex optimization. Furthermore, we extend the analysis of various line segment. Finally, we show that, in the case of a closed escape path for the unit strip, the optimal solution is a curve of constant unit width.
tldr: This paper solves a geometric optimization problem related to Bellman's Lost-in-a-Forest Problem, specifically the escape path for an infinite unit-strip forest and unit broadworm.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a new computational approach to a classic geometric problem that was previously solved only by geometric methods.
method: The problem is reformulated as an interval-cover problem and then as a constrained functional minimization problem, which is discretized and solved via convex optimization.
result: Analytical formulas for the escape path are derived, and it is shown that the optimal solution for a closed escape path in the unit strip is a curve of constant unit width.
conclusion: The work extends previous geometric solutions with a computational framework, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fragility Of Minimum-Variance Portfolios
authors: Daniel Ovalle, Carl D. Laird, Ignacio E. Grossmann, Javier Pe\~na
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum-variance portfolios are well known to be highly sensitive to covariance estimation error. In this paper, we show that by imposing a block diagonal correlation structure, we can derive closed-form expressions for long-only minimum-variance portfolios that make this fragility explicit. These analytical solutions reveal that fragility is driven by threshold effects arising from the interaction between correlation structure and the assets' volatilities. Motivated by the latter insight, we propose robustification approaches that can be interpreted as structured shrinkage schemes that selectively attenuate unstable coupling while preserving the dominant risk structure. Unlike global shrinkage techniques, the proposed corrections are analytically grounded, require minimal tuning, and remain closely aligned with the minimum-variance solution. The framework extends naturally to general covariance matrices through clustering-based approximations. Empirical results on controlled simulations highlight a clear regime dependence. In homogeneous volatility settings, correlation-oblivious shrinkage achieves the best trade-off between risk and stability. In contrast, under heterogeneous volatility, correlation-aware shrinkage performs best by inducing sparsity and avoiding exposure to high-risk assets. Across regimes, the proposed methods consistently reduce out-of-sample variance and turnover relative to classical and clustering-based benchmarks, providing a principled and practical approach to robust portfolio construction.
tldr: This paper studies fragility of minimum-variance portfolios in finance, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Minimum-variance portfolios are sensitive to covariance estimation error, and the authors aim to understand and mitigate this fragility.
method: Closed-form expressions for long-only minimum-variance portfolios under block diagonal correlation structure are derived, and robustification approaches based on structured shrinkage are proposed.
result: Analytical solutions reveal threshold effects; correlation-aware shrinkage performs best under heterogeneous volatility, while correlation-oblivious shrinkage works in homogeneous settings.
conclusion: The proposed methods reduce out-of-sample variance and turnover, providing a principled approach to robust portfolio construction.

title: A Lecture On Navier-Stokes Equations

method: The lecture covers Fourier transform, Sobolev spaces, nonlinear heat equation as a toy model, and then proves existence and uniqueness of mild solutions for Navier-Stokes in critical spaces.
result: The paper presents a pedagogical exposition with exercises and exams, culminating in a proof of existence and uniqueness of mild solutions.

title: Learning Sufficient Low-dimensional Structures Through Conditional Optimal Transport
authors: Efstathia Bura Kaiqiang Alan Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sufficient dimension reduction seeks a low-dimensional covariate representation that preserves the conditional law of a response. We introduce SDR-COT, which represents that law by conditional optimal transport from an independent reference response. On separable Hilbert spaces, sufficiency forces the response component of the optimal triangular map to factor through the reduction. For quadratic cost, the induced interpolation has a Borel current-state velocity on every truncated time interval, without global injectivity of the terminal map, and this velocity has the same factorisation. These results motivate a conditional-flow-matching criterion. For linear reductions, we prove consistency using a suitably tuned relaxed empirical coupling. Euclidean responses are treated through slicewise Caffarelli bounds; Hilbert-valued responses are treated through Gaussian Sobolev regularity, interpolation compression and uniqueness of a Gaussian continuity equation. Numerical studies with Euclidean and functional data show competitive performance, especially when sufficient information is not solely contained in the conditional mean.
tldr: This paper introduces a method for sufficient dimension reduction using conditional optimal transport, with theoretical guarantees on Hilbert spaces.
motivation: To find low-dimensional representations of covariates that preserve the conditional distribution of a response, which is a classical problem in statistics.
method: The authors propose SDR-COT, which represents the conditional law via optimal transport from an independent reference, and use a conditional flow matching criterion for estimation.
result: They prove that sufficiency forces factorization through the reduction, and establish consistency for linear reductions using relaxed empirical coupling.
conclusion: The method shows competitive performance on Euclidean and functional data, especially when sufficient information is not solely in the conditional mean.

title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Aided Isac: User Fairness Optimization And Performance Evaluation
authors: Hailun Huang, Yuwen Cao, Jiguang He, Tomoaki Ohtsuki
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates max-min user fairness optimization for flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with active self-localization. To tackle the multi-user interference, performance imbalance, and neglected sensing accuracy problems encountered in conventional ISAC designs, we derive the closed-form Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for angle-of-departure (AoD) estimation in target sensing and embed it into a max-min fairness optimization framework. The optimization problem, which jointly designs the base station transmit beamforming, FIM reflection coefficients, and surface deformation, is non-convex and solved by an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Notably, the devised optimization framework facilitates superior performance trade-off in terms of spectrum resource utilization between communication and sensing tasks. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme significantly improves user fairness, balances communication performance and sensing precision effectively, and reveals the coupling characteristic between signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and sensing CRLB. This work provides a feasible solution for FIM-aided ISAC system optimization in 6G networks.
tldr: This paper optimizes user fairness in FIM-NOMA-ISAC systems for 6G networks using alternating optimization.
motivation: Conventional ISAC designs suffer from multi-user interference, performance imbalance, and neglected sensing accuracy.
method: Derives closed-form CRLB for AoD estimation and embeds it into a max-min fairness optimization framework solved by alternating optimization.
result: The proposed scheme significantly improves user fairness and balances communication performance with sensing precision.
conclusion: Provides a feasible solution for FIM-aided ISAC system optimization in 6G networks.

title: A Frugal Primal-dual Splitting With Minimal Lifting Over Arbitrary Rooted Trees
authors: Hui Zhang Feng Xue
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a frugal primal-dual splitting with minimal lifting for solving structured monotone inclusions, involving cocoercive operators, linear compositions and parallel sums. This is established by defining hierarchical nodes and edges between them over a tree-structured graph, with arbitrary assignments of dual variables and cocoercive elements to primal nodes. This arbitrariness allows a great flexibility in terms of level-synchronous distributed computing, such as centralized or decentralized. The particular instances naturally extend the Douglas--Rachford splitting on various graphs, recover the parallel Chambolle--Pock, and solve a class of structured convex minimization problems with O(1/k) ergodic rate for its primal-dual gap function. Furthermore, we introduce a reformulation technique in a product Hilbert space to facilitate the convergence analysis, specifically to derive the o(1/k)-rate of asymptotic regularity.
tldr: This paper develops a frugal primal-dual splitting algorithm for solving structured monotone inclusions on tree-structured graphs.
motivation: To design a flexible distributed optimization algorithm with minimal lifting that can handle cocoercive operators and linear compositions.
method: The authors define hierarchical nodes and edges over a tree graph, assign dual variables and cocoercive elements arbitrarily to primal nodes, and use a reformulation in product Hilbert space for convergence analysis.
result: The algorithm achieves O(1/k) ergodic rate for the primal-dual gap and o(1/k) asymptotic regularity, generalizing Douglas-Rachford splitting and Chambolle-Pock.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a flexible framework for distributed convex optimization with proven convergence rates.

title: Characterizing The Dynamics Of Muscle Regeneration In The Mdx Mouse Model
authors: Elena Scibona, Davide Carbone, Lamberto Rondoni, Abramo Agosti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we explore a model of immune response in the skeletal muscle of the mdx mouse, the preferred animal model for studying Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. The system studied is based on existing literature and describes the reaction of the tissue, and of the immune cells within it, to external damage, focusing specifically on the regeneration process. This work extends the analysis conducted by the authors of the original paper, highlighting interesting dynamical properties of the system, particularly in terms of longterm behavior and dependence on initial conditions. A modification is then introduced to the original equations, incorporating a diffusion term for immune cells. The dynamics of the system is numerically investigated in both the one-dimensional and two-dimensional cases. Specifically, we investigate the effect of diffusion under various boundary conditions, and the system's response to localized damage.
tldr: This paper models immune response and muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, focusing on dynamical properties and diffusion effects.
motivation: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy is a severe muscle-wasting disease, and understanding the dynamics of muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model can inform therapeutic strategies.
method: The authors extend an existing model by adding a diffusion term for immune cells and numerically investigate the system's dynamics in 1D and 2D under various boundary conditions and localized damage.
result: The study reveals interesting long-term behavior and dependence on initial conditions, and shows how diffusion affects the regeneration process.
conclusion: The modified model captures key aspects of muscle regeneration dynamics, providing insights that could guide future experimental and theoretical work.

title: A Refined Structure Theorem For Polynomial Return-time Sets In Minimal Systems
authors: Ioannis Kousek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a refinement of a recent structural result in topological dynamics due to Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, Le, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, who showed that in a minimal system, polynomial return-times differ by non-piecewise syndetic sets from those in its maximal infinite-step pronilfactor. In particular, we prove that the infinite-step pronilfactor can be replaced by the maximal [MATH]-step pronilfactor of the system, where [MATH] depends only on the given polynomials, with [MATH] equal to the Host-Kra complexity of the polynomials.

title: Graphical Stability Of Set-valued Integrals Under Measure Perturbations
authors: Tam Le
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by sampling and approximation schemes arising in nonsmooth optimization, we study the stability of parameterized set-valued integrals under weak perturbations of the underlying probability distribution. For a compact parameter set, we show that compact convex-valued and jointly outer semicontinuous integrands induce set-valued integral maps that converge graphically in excess distance along any weakly convergent sequence of probability measures. The result holds under a superlinear integrability condition and provides a unified stability principle for measure approximations of set-valued expectations. We discuss the sharpness of the assumptions through examples. In particular, we emphasize that joint outer semicontinuity is required in general and that the superlinear envelope condition is tight relative to the classical i.i.d. empirical setting. As a consequence, we obtain outer stability of solution sets for stochastic generalized equations. We illustrate the stability result in several settings, including stochastic nonsmooth optimization with Markovian sampling, smoothing by mollifiers, and parameter-dependent distributional dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of set-valued integrals under measure perturbations, with applications in nonsmooth optimization.
motivation: To provide a unified stability principle for measure approximations of set-valued expectations, motivated by sampling and approximation schemes in nonsmooth optimization.
method: The authors prove that compact convex-valued and jointly outer semicontinuous integrands induce set-valued integral maps that converge graphically in excess distance along weakly convergent sequences of probability measures, under a superlinear integrability condition.
result: The result holds under a superlinear integrability condition and is sharp; it yields outer stability of solution sets for stochastic generalized equations.
conclusion: The stability result is illustrated in stochastic nonsmooth optimization with Markovian sampling, smoothing by mollifiers, and parameter-dependent distributional dynamics.

title: On The Performance Of Fluid Antenna Systems Under Block-Diagonal Correlation Model
authors: Jiangsheng Huangfu, Zhengyu Song, Tianwei Hou, Anna Li, Kai Kit Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have recently emerged as a promising reconfigurable antenna technology for future wireless networks, owing to their unique ability to exploit fine-grained spatial channel variations within a compact aperture. In this paper, a single-input multiple-output (SIMO) FAS employing maximum-ratio combining (MRC) is investigated under the block-diagonal correlation model, where the ports of FAS are partitioned into independent blocks and the strongest port within each block is selected for MRC combining. Exact outage probability (OP) expressions are first derived in both convolution and characteristic-function forms. To gain further insights, closed-form high-SNR asymptotic expressions are developed, from which the diversity order is shown to approximate the number of ports. This result reveals that block partitioning influences only the coding gain and can therefore be optimized without compromising the diversity performance. For the ergodic rate (ER), a Gamma-matching approximation together with a tighter Jensen-based approximation is derived in closed form. Simulation results corroborate the analytical framework and demonstrate that: i) increasing either the number of ports or the number of blocks improves the system performance; ii) the diversity order depends solely on the number of ports; and iii) the proposed SIMO-FAS achieves comparable or superior outage performance to conventional MRC receivers despite employing fewer combining branches.
tldr: This paper analyzes the performance of fluid antenna systems under a block-diagonal correlation model for wireless communications.
motivation: Fluid antenna systems are a promising reconfigurable antenna technology for future wireless networks, and understanding their performance under realistic correlation models is important.
method: The authors derive exact outage probability expressions and closed-form high-SNR asymptotic expressions for a SIMO-FAS with MRC, and also derive Gamma-matching and Jensen-based approximations for ergodic rate.
result: The diversity order approximates the number of ports, block partitioning affects only coding gain, and increasing ports or blocks improves performance.
conclusion: The proposed SIMO-FAS achieves comparable or superior outage performance to conventional MRC receivers with fewer combining branches.

title: Industrial Application Of A Multi-Disciplinary Design Optimization With Uncertainties To A Pair Of Telecommunication Satellites
authors: Olivier Sapin (ADS), Lo\"ic Cousin (ADS), Nicolas Roussouly (ADS), Anne Gazaix (ADS), Fran\c{c}ois Gallard (ADS), Matthias de Lozzo (ADS), Xavier Fosse (ADS), Nicolas Sarda (ADS), Gaspard Berthelin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In satellite design, it is common practice to add safety margins to the constraints to achieve conservative solutions that are robust to uncertainties. This robustness often comes at the expense of performance and it may be more appropriate to include uncertainties in the definition of the design problem. This work addresses such a challenge by applying techniques of multidisciplinary design optimization under uncertainty to an industrial use case. The latter is a pair of telecommunication satellites launched together in a stacked configuration. Each satellite is a strongly coupled multidisciplinary system while the two satellites are not coupled at all. This use case can be extended to an arbitrary number of satellites. By considering uncertainty quantification techniques such as sensitivity analysis and reliability-based design optimization, this study demonstrates that accounting for uncertainties in the design problem results in a 66% reduction in performance loss compared to the adding of a predefined safety margins, while guaranteeing the feasibility of constraints with high probability.
tldr: This paper applies multidisciplinary design optimization under uncertainty to telecommunication satellite design, demonstrating a 66% reduction in performance loss compared to traditional safety margins.
motivation: In satellite design, safety margins are commonly used to ensure robustness against uncertainties, but this often sacrifices performance. The authors aim to incorporate uncertainties directly into the design optimization to achieve better performance while maintaining reliability.
method: The authors employ uncertainty quantification techniques including sensitivity analysis and reliability-based design optimization on a pair of telecommunication satellites launched in a stacked configuration, treating each satellite as a strongly coupled multidisciplinary system.
result: The proposed approach reduces performance loss by 66% compared to using predefined safety margins, while still guaranteeing constraint feasibility with high probability.
conclusion: Accounting for uncertainties in the design problem can significantly improve performance over traditional safety margin approaches, and the methodology can be extended to an arbitrary number of satellites.

title: Decentralized Linearized Consensus Admm With Efficient Quantized Communication
authors: Boyu Han, Xu Du, Karl H. Johansson, Apostolos I. Rikos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed optimization offers significant advantages over centralized methods in terms of scalability and robustness when solving large-scale problems. In this paper, we propose a novel decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates Inexact Consensus ADMM (IC-ADMM) with a finite-time decentralized quantized communication algorithm. The proposed method enjoys three main benefits: (i) it operates on directed communication graphs, (ii) it requires only quantized local information instead of exact values, and (iii) it does not rely on solving the local subproblems exactly. Under the assumption that each node's local objective is strongly convex and L-smooth, the algorithm is guaranteed to achieve global linear convergence to a neighborhood of the optimal solution. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate its advantages over existing methods in terms of convergence speed and communication efficiency.

motivation: Distributed optimization faces challenges in communication efficiency and robustness; existing methods often require exact information or undirected graphs.
method: The algorithm integrates Inexact Consensus ADMM with a finite-time decentralized quantized communication scheme, allowing directed graphs and quantized local information.
result: Under strong convexity and L-smoothness assumptions, the algorithm achieves global linear convergence to a neighborhood of the optimal solution.
conclusion: The proposed method improves convergence speed and communication efficiency over existing approaches, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: Identifiability, Convergence And Nonparametric Estimation Of Bivariate Archimax Copulas
authors: Wolfgang Trutschnig Nicolas Dietrich
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Considering that the family of bivariate Archimax copulas contains both the Archimedean and the extreme-value class, Archimax copulas constitute a flexible family allowing to model extreme and moderate levels of dependence. We resolve this identifiability issue by working with transformed generators and transformed Pickands dependence functions, and show that these functions do identify the Archimax copula uniquely. Building upon this result, we prove that uniform convergence of Archimax copulas is equivalent to uniform convergence of the corresponding transformed generators and Pickands dependence functions. Moreover, as for Archimedean and extreme-value copulas, uniform convergence in [MATH] is equivalent to weak convergence of almost all conditional distributions. Exploiting these equivalences, we construct two nonparametric estimators for Archimax copulas (a Pickands and a CFG type estimator, both elements of [MATH]) and show that they are strongly consistent under mild regularity conditions. As a further consequence of the aforementioned weak conditional convergence, we obtain strongly consistent plug-in estimators for measures of directed dependence such as Chatterjee's [MATH] and Trutschnig's [MATH]. A large-scale simulation study shows that the proposed CFG type estimator outperforms both the standard empirical copula estimator and the Pickands type estimator; an application to precipitation data from Bregenz and Dornbirn (Austria) illustrates the practical use of our estimators on real data.

title: Space-time Tensor-product Finite Element Methods For Parabolic Problems
authors: Richard L\"oscher, Michael Reichelt, Olaf Steinbach
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study space-time Galerkin--Petrov formulations for parabolic evolution problems and their relation to classical implicit time-stepping schemes. Although such schemes are stable in the usual time-stepping sense, their interpretation as space-time operator equations may lead to conditional stability, with constants depending on the relation between temporal and spatial mesh sizes. We revisit this phenomenon for the continuous Galerkin method of Aziz and Monk, which yields the Crank--Nicolson scheme in the lowest-order case, and provide a detailed space-time error analysis for solutions of both high and low regularity. In particular, the space-time framework allows us to analyze the deteriorated behaviour of classical time-stepping methods for nonsmooth initial data. By applying integration by parts in time, we derive an adjoint space-time formulation that incorporates the initial condition in a natural variational way. In the lowest-order case, this formulation leads to a Rannacher-type smoothing of the initial data. The theoretical results are complemented by numerical experiments.

motivation: Classical time-stepping schemes for parabolic problems can exhibit conditional stability when interpreted as space-time operator equations, motivating a unified space-time framework.

result: The space-time framework reveals deteriorated behavior for nonsmooth initial data and leads to a Rannacher-type smoothing in the lowest-order case.
conclusion: Space-time formulations provide a rigorous error analysis and can improve the treatment of initial conditions in parabolic problems.
